Hint and option on dg_site: tissue beside an organ, such as peripancreatic tissue, does not name the organ; the option's reason states that ICD-O lists peripancreatic and retrocaecal tissue under retroperitoneum (C48.0).

Hint and options on dg_site: overlapping lesions take .8 (colon C18.8; rectum, anus and anal canal C21.8; biliary tract C24.8; digestive system C26.8); a carcinoma of oesophagus and stomach is indexed to cardia C16.0. Each reason names the code.
Referral only: the lymphoma options refer to Group 2, which applies Rule D to the topography.

Hint on dg_net_grade: if the report gives two grades, or the Ki-67 index and mitotic count point to different grades, choose the higher (Nagtegaal 2020 Table 2 footnote states the same rule). The sixth digit is not built.

conflicts.issue: ICCC-2017 places cholangiocarcinoma, bile duct cystadenocarcinoma and perihilar cholangiocarcinoma in VIIb at every site, so a bile duct carcinoma of the gallbladder or extrahepatic bile ducts goes to Group 7, though those sites are XIf10 for other carcinomas and REDCap lists the codes in Group 11.

Pancreatoblastoma is ICCC XIIa2 at every site; the pancreas screen refers it to Group 12.
Gastrointestinal stromal tumour is ICCC XIIa1; the stomach, small intestine, oesophagus and colorectal screens refer it to Group 12.
Tissue-free registration (basis 1 or 2) records 8000/3, which ICCC-2017 places in XIIb at every digestive site. The ICCC subgroup computed at output is XIIb, not XI.
Gastroblastoma is a biphasic epithelial and spindle-cell tumour with no code in ICD-O-3.2 or ICCC-2017; whether it belongs in Group 11 or Group 12 is the registrar's ruling.
8452 is /3 at the pancreas (Group 11) and /1 at the ovary (out of scope, a Group 10 site). The behaviour follows the site.
Hepatoid adenocarcinoma and yolk sac tumour-like carcinoma of the stomach express alpha fetoprotein; a hepatoid yolk sac tumour (9071/3) is ICCC Xb4. The histology report's tumour name decides.
Lymphomas (Burkitt lymphoma 9687/3 is ICCC IIc) and EBV-positive inflammatory follicular dendritic cell sarcoma (9758/3, ICCC IId) of the digestive tract refer to Group 2.

data_gaps.why: Nagtegaal 2020 is a commentary and prints no entity table. Without it the picker cannot name medullary carcinoma (8510/3 Medullary carcinoma, NOS), adenoma-like adenocarcinoma, high-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm, ampullary intestinal and pancreatobiliary types (8144/3, 8163/3), or the pancreatic carcinoma subtypes, and the colorectal exclusion screen cannot be checked against WHO terms.
data_gaps.candidate_source: The ICCR histopathology reporting guides for colorectal cancer, carcinoma of the exocrine pancreas, ampulla of Vater, gallbladder and bile ducts (each prints the WHO 5th-edition table with ICD-O codes).

data_gaps.need: Diagnostic criteria and immunohistochemistry for pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma and pancreatoblastoma in children, and for paediatric pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours.
data_gaps.why: Pfister 2022 names acinar cell carcinoma and pancreatoblastoma but gives no criteria, and no paper added on 8 October 2026 reports acinar cell carcinoma in a child. Karges 2025 reports the occurrence, grade and function of paediatric pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours but gives no immunohistochemistry criteria. The pancreas checklist keeps one rule (solid pseudopapillary neoplasm) and no recognition aid for acinar cell carcinoma.
data_gaps.candidate_source: The EXPeRT/PARTNER recommendations for pancreatic tumours in children and adolescents (Pediatric Blood & Cancer 2021, supplement; controller to verify).

data_gaps.need: Whether goblet cell adenocarcinoma, appendiceal mucinous neoplasms and grade 3 appendiceal neuroendocrine tumours occur before age 19.
data_gaps.why: Roganovic 2026 settles the frequency and grading of paediatric appendiceal neuroendocrine tumours: the most frequent gastrointestinal epithelial tumour of children, mostly grade 1, grade 2 rare. It reports no grade 3 tumour in a child; the grade 3 option rests on Pfister 2022's listing of appendiceal neuroendocrine tumours, and the controller decides whether it stays. Goblet cell adenocarcinoma, low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm and mucinous adenocarcinoma of the appendix have no paediatric report.
data_gaps.candidate_source: A paediatric appendiceal neuroendocrine tumour series or the EXPeRT/PARTNER neuroendocrine neoplasm recommendations (controller to verify).

data_gaps.need: A serum or urine test that the digestive sources give a diagnostic role.
data_gaps.why: No file in this part names one. The marker screen rests only on the registrar's Visser 2023 Table 4 rule. The papers added on 8 October 2026 give no marker a diagnostic role: Roganovic 2026 states that raised urinary 5-HIAA, chromogranin A or neuron-specific enolase has not been described in children with appendiceal neuroendocrine tumours, Mahajan 2022 that the role of carcinoembryonic antigen in paediatric colorectal carcinoma is not established, and Karges 2025 defines a functioning tumour by a clinical syndrome with hormone abnormalities, not by immunohistochemistry alone.

data_gaps.need: The ICD-O code of malignant gastrointestinal neuroectodermal tumour.
data_gaps.why: Nagtegaal 2020 names it with gastrointestinal clear cell sarcoma; ICD-O-3.2 has no term for it, so its referral group is unverified. The sarcoma option covers it until the registrar rules.
data_gaps.candidate_source: WHO Digestive System Tumours, 5th ed., 2019, mesenchymal tumours chapter.

data_gaps.need: A ruling on whether the colorectal options apply at the anus and anal canal (C21.0 to C21.8).
data_gaps.why: dg_colorectal_histology serves the colon, rectosigmoid junction, rectum and anus. The five new colorectal options rest on colon, rectosigmoid and rectal carcinomas in children (Polat 2021, Mahajan 2022); no paper reports anal carcinoma in a child. Their entities list C18.0, C18.2 to C18.9, C19.9 and C20.9, while the screen still shows them for an anal tumour; the anal sites stay on the picker entities.

data_gaps.need: A paediatric report of colorectal tubular adenocarcinoma as the only histological type.
data_gaps.why: The tubular adenocarcinoma option rests on one tumour with mucinous and tubular adenocarcinoma components in a 16-year-old (Polat 2021 Table 1, PMC section 2), which records 8480/3 under the higher-code rule. The controller decides whether the option stays on the colorectal screen or returns to the picker.

data_gaps.need: An immunohistochemistry rule for a solid pseudopapillary neoplasm without nuclear beta-catenin.
data_gaps.why: Ebrahim 2025 reports a boy whose solid pseudopapillary neoplasm lacked nuclear beta-catenin, and higher CD99 and LEF1 expression in the four paediatric cases (PMC section 13). The single dg_pancreas_ihc rule requires nuclear beta-catenin, so such a tumour reaches 8000/3 when the report names no type, and the recognition aid on the solid pseudopapillary neoplasm option names nuclear beta-catenin. The controller decides whether to add a CD99 and LEF1 rule.
